input.strategy_title: Integrated GenAI model evaluation for RHOAI
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers adopting generative models on RHOAI have no supported way to answer
"is this model good enough for my use case?" inside the platform. Evaluation
today happens in ad-hoc notebooks with lm-evaluation-harness or vendor tools,
results live in spreadsheets, and nothing links an evaluation to the model
version that was actually deployed. We need a first-class evaluation capability:
run standard and custom benchmarks against models served on the platform,
persist results alongside the model version, and let users compare candidates
before promoting one to production.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | Users can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite. |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Standard benchmark suites (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag exposed through lm-eval task names) are available out of the box. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | Evaluation results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Users can define custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics) and run them through the same flow. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | The Dashboard shows evaluation runs, their status, and per-benchmark scores, and allows side-by-side comparison of two model versions. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | Evaluations can be embedded as a step in a Data Science Pipeline so promotion flows can gate on scores. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Llama Stack's eval provider API is backed by the platform evaluation service, so agents/apps built on Llama Stack get the same results. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Evaluation runs record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for capacity planning. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Product documentation covers the evaluation workflow end to end, including custom task authoring. |

## Affected Components

- TrustyAI
- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry

## Out of Scope

- Human-preference (arena style) evaluation collection
- Automatic model promotion decisions — pipelines gate, humans promote
- Fine-tuning feedback loops driven by evaluation scores

## Open Questions

1. Execution engine: TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview) already wraps
   lm-evaluation-harness — do we build on it as the single execution path, or is
   a new evaluation service needed to also serve Llama Stack's eval provider
   API? Needs a technical investigation with a recommendation.
2. Result schema: what is the canonical result format persisted to Model
   Registry custom properties, and does it survive benchmark-suite version
   bumps? Prototype against real MMLU output before committing.
3. Benchmark dataset licensing: which standard suites can we redistribute in
   disconnected environments, and which must be fetched by the customer?

# TrustyAI: Extend LMEvalJob into the platform evaluation execution path

## Description

Branch outcome A of the execution engine investigation: build on TrustyAI's
LMEvalJob (Tech Preview, wrapping lm-evaluation-harness) as the single
execution path for platform model evaluation. Users launch evaluations of
models served on the platform (KServe endpoints or Llama Stack distributions)
against standard benchmark suites; results are emitted in the canonical result
schema, written through the Model Registry persistence contract and linked to
the evaluated model's registered version, and each run records cost/duration
metadata. Custom evaluation tasks (user-defined datasets and metrics) are
delivered by a follow-on P1 epic in this branch, deferred independently of
this P0 core. This epic
applies if the investigation recommends extending LMEvalJob; if it recommends
a new evaluation service instead, this epic is replaced by the alternative
branch's service implementation.

## Scope

- Extend the LMEvalJob path so an evaluation can be launched against a model
  served on a KServe endpoint or a Llama Stack distribution, with a selected
  benchmark suite.
- Deliver the out-of-the-box standard suite set (lm-eval task names) fixed by
  the benchmark licensing classification: suites classified redistributable
  are bundled for disconnected environments; customer-fetched suites have a
  documented fetch path.
- Emit results in the canonical result schema and write them through the Model
  Registry persistence and linking contract (owned by the Model Registry
  persistence work), which links them to the evaluated model's registered
  version; this epic does not implement its own result storage.
- Record cost/duration metadata on each run: tokens, wall-clock time, and GPU
  time.
- Carry the LMEvalJob capability from Tech Preview toward supported status as
  part of hardening it into the platform execution path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe
  endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite,
  and observe the run's status while it executes.
- Standard suites classified as redistributable are available out of the box in
  a disconnected environment; suites classified customer-fetched can be
  retrieved by the customer via the documented path.
- Results are emitted in the canonical result schema, written through the
  Model Registry persistence contract, and linked to the evaluated model's
  Model Registry version.
- Every run records cost/duration metadata: tokens, wall-clock, and GPU time.
- Existing LMEvalJob usage is not broken by the extension (backward
  compatibility for the Tech Preview surface).
- Changed repositories' build pipelines are green.

## HLR Traceability

HLR-1 (P0): launch an evaluation of a served model against a selected suite.
HLR-2 (P0): standard benchmark suites available out of the box. HLR-8 (P2):
cost/duration metadata per run — bundled with the P0 work because it falls out
of the same run record. HLR-4 (P1, custom evaluation tasks) is covered by the
follow-on custom-task epic in this branch, split out so it can be deferred
independently of the P0 core.

## Risks / Notes

- LMEvalJob is Tech Preview; hardening it into the supported execution path is
  part of this epic's cost, and the investigation's recommendation must have
  weighed it.
- The single-gate schema records only the execution-engine existence gate;
  this epic's suite-delivery scope is also materially conditioned on the
  benchmark licensing classification (redistributable vs. customer-fetched)
  and on the canonical result schema from the upstream investigations, both
  carried as plain build-against dependencies.

Branch outcome A of the execution engine investigation: wire a production eval
provider into the platform's Llama Stack distribution, backed by the TrustyAI
LMEvalJob execution path, so agents and apps built on Llama Stack get the same

## Scope

- Implement and configure the Llama Stack eval provider plugin for the platform
  distribution, backed by the platform evaluation service surface exposed by
  the TrustyAI execution path.
- Map the eval provider API onto platform evaluation launches and results:
  benchmark suite selection maps to the platform's suite set, and returned
  results use the canonical result schema.
- Make the provider available in LlamaStackDistribution deployments without
  custom user wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack app or agent using the eval provider API receives results
  consistent with the platform evaluation flow for the same model and suite.
- The provider is available in platform Llama Stack distributions by default,
  requiring no custom user configuration.
- Provider-level errors map sensibly to platform evaluation failures (run
  failures surface as provider errors, not silent empty results).

## HLR Traceability

HLR-7 (P1): Llama Stack's eval provider API is backed by the platform
evaluation service, so agents/apps built on Llama Stack get the same results.

## Risks / Notes

- If the provider cannot be carried entirely in the midstream distribution,
  coordination with upstream Llama Stack (meta-llama/llama-stack) may be
  needed; treat that as a risk to escalate, not a reason to redesign the
  platform-side wiring.

# TrustyAI: Custom evaluation tasks on the LMEvalJob execution path

## Description

Branch outcome A of the execution engine investigation, follow-on to the
execution-path epic: users can define custom evaluation tasks — their own
datasets and metrics — and run them through the same platform evaluation flow
built on the extended LMEvalJob capability. Custom task support is a distinct,
deferrable feature (P1): it is split from the P0 launch/execution core so the
standard-suite capability can ship without it, and this epic extends the
existing execution surface via a dependency rather than rebuilding it. This
epic applies if the investigation recommends extending LMEvalJob; if it
recommends a new evaluation service instead, this epic is replaced by the
alternative branch's custom-task epic.

## Scope

- Support user-defined evaluation tasks — custom datasets and custom metrics —
  registered through lm-evaluation-harness's custom-task mechanism and launched
  through the same flow as the out-of-the-box standard suites.
- Accept user-supplied task definitions (dataset and metric) without changes to
  the execution path's deployment or serving configuration.
- Emit custom-task results in the canonical result schema, written through the
  Model Registry persistence and linking contract so they are linked to the
  evaluated model's registered version alongside standard-suite results.
- Record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) on custom-task
  runs, using the same run record as standard-suite runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can define a custom evaluation task (own dataset, own metric) and
  launch it against a model served on the platform through the same flow used
  for standard suites.
- A custom-task run's status is observable while it executes, like a
  standard-suite run.
- Custom-task results are persisted in the canonical result schema, linked to
  the evaluated model's Model Registry version, with cost/duration metadata
  recorded.
- Defining a custom task requires no change to the execution path's deployment
  or serving configuration.
- Changed repositories' build pipelines are green.

## HLR Traceability

HLR-4 (P1): users can define custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and
metrics) and run them through the same flow. Split from the P0 execution epic
so it can be deferred independently of the standard-suite launch/execution
core; it extends the execution surface that epic delivers.

## Risks / Notes

- User-supplied datasets and metrics may need validation/sandboxing
  considerations on the execution path; carried inside this epic.
- The single-gate schema records only the execution-engine existence gate;
  this epic also builds against the canonical result schema and the Model

  carried as its dependency chain.
